Polysaccharides have 1000 or more sugar units and high molecular weights. In plants, many are glucose polymers that either
provide stored energy, usually as starch, or materials for structural plant components (e.g., celluloses and hemicelluloses). Starch
chains are formed when glucose, not needed immediately by the plant, is shuttled to amyloplasts for polymerization. Starch chains
align into starch granules whose shape, size, organization, crystallinity, number, and location (e.g., roots, rhizomes, seeds, stems,
tubers and corms) and amylose: amylopectin ratio are determined by plant type and variety.
